name: mutate-config
description: Phase 1 (fleshed from the Phase-0 seed) — apply exactly ONE edit to a parent config bundle, producing a candidate (PLAN.md §2.3 / IMPLEMENTATION.md §2.3). Runs inline as a `command` (shares the session; cannot change model). Flow: SETUP copies the parent bundle into out_dir + emits its manifest/file-tree -> RESOLVE_IDEA reads the idea text by id from research-ideas.md -> PLAN_EDIT (prompt, output_schema) picks the single edit -> APPLY (prompt, uses file tools) makes exactly that edit inside out_dir -> STAMP merges the lineage fields (id/parent_id/idea_id) into out_dir/manifest.json, preserving APPLY's change. Single-edit discipline keeps lineages attributable.

arguments.name: parent_id
arguments.description: id of the parent bundle to mutate ($1)

arguments.name: idea_id
arguments.description: id of the mutation idea to apply, resolved from research-ideas.md ($2)

arguments.name: out_dir
arguments.description: absolute path of the working dir to write the candidate bundle into ($3)

setup.name: SETUP_COPY_PARENT
setup.command:
set -eu
AR="${AUTORES_ROOT:-/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch}"
PARENT="$AR/dict/configs/$1"
test -f "$PARENT/manifest.json" || { echo "mutate-config: parent bundle not found: $PARENT" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$3"
cp -a "$PARENT/." "$3/"
echo "=== parent manifest ($1) ==="
cat "$PARENT/manifest.json"
echo "=== candidate file tree ($3) ==="
( cd "$3" && find . -type f | sort )

resolve_idea.name: RESOLVE_IDEA
resolve_idea.command:
set -eu
AR="${AUTORES_ROOT:-/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch}"
IDEAS="$AR/research-ideas.md"
if [ -f "$IDEAS" ] && grep -qF "$2" "$IDEAS"; then
  grep -F "$2" "$IDEAS" | head -1 | sed -E 's/^- \[[ x]\] *//'
else
  echo "$2"
  echo "mutate-config: idea id '$2' not found in $IDEAS; using the id itself as the idea text (hand-run/hardcoded path)" >&2
fi

plan_edit.name: PLAN_EDIT
plan_edit.prompt:
<sys>
You are mutating a config bundle for an autoresearch optimizer. Below is the parent bundle's manifest and file tree, and one mutation idea. Propose EXACTLY ONE concrete edit that applies the idea — a single knob, so the experiment's effect is attributable.

Parent bundle context:
{{parent_ctx}}

Mutation idea ({{idea_text}}):
Choose ONE target:
- model: swap manifest.main_model, or one entry of manifest.spawn_block_models
- flowchart: edit one block in one flowchart/*.json file
- kb: edit kb/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md or one kb/refs/*.md file
- extension: toggle one entry of manifest.extensions[]

Emit the single edit as structured output. Be concrete: for a model swap, `path` is the manifest field (e.g. "manifest.main_model") and `change` is the exact new value.
</sys>

target.description: one of: model | flowchart | kb | extension

path.description: the file or manifest field the edit targets

change.description: the concrete change to apply (for a model swap, the exact new model id)

rationale.description: why this edit, tied to the idea

apply.name: APPLY_EDIT
apply.prompt:
<sys>
Apply EXACTLY this one edit to the candidate bundle at $3 (already a copy of the parent). Change ONLY this and nothing else.

  target:   {{target}}
  path:     {{path}}
  change:   {{change}}
  rationale:{{rationale}}

Use your file tools (Read/Edit/Write) plus Bash. Rules:
- model edits: edit the JSON field in $3/manifest.json (main_model or the named spawn_block_models entry). Keep valid JSON.
- flowchart/kb edits: edit the named file under $3/. Preserve JSON validity for flowchart files.
- extension edits: edit manifest.extensions[].
After applying, print a one-line confirmation of the before/after value. Do not touch manifest.id / parent_id / idea_id (the next step stamps those).
</sys>

stamp.name: STAMP_MANIFEST
stamp.command:
set -eu
OUT="$3"
CAND_ID="$(basename "$OUT")"
PY=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/.venv/bin/python
"$PY" - "$OUT/manifest.json" "$CAND_ID" "$1" "$2" <<'PYEOF'
import json, sys
path, cand_id, parent_id, idea_id = sys.argv[1:5]
m = json.load(open(path))
m["id"] = cand_id
m["parent_id"] = parent_id
m["idea_id"] = idea_id
json.dump(m, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
PYEOF
echo "$CAND_ID"
